explanation: The Calvin cycle is a cyclical series of reactions that takes place in the stroma of chloroplasts. It utilizes atmospheric carbon dioxide to produce carbohydrates. This pathway is also known as C3 photosynthesis. The Calvin cycle involves three distinct, sequential stages: 1) Carbon dioxide fixation, where CO2 is captured; 2) Carbon dioxide reduction, where the carbon compounds are reduced; and 3) Ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate (RuBP) regeneration, which resets the cycle to accept more CO2.
